messages:
marco (eng-infra): FYI saw a bunch of GPU training pods stuck Pending for ~10m while CA spun up nodes in us-east instead of eu-west. Strange cross-zone behavior.
priya (eng-infra): ugh, same. pods have zoneAffinity eu-west1 and nodeSelector for gpu-type: a100, but autoscaler picked us-east nodegroup weights?
marco (eng-infra): here's the relevant autoscaler log snippet from last scale event:
```
I0503 12:22:11.123456 autoscaler.go:123] Scaling up: triggered by 8 unschedulable pods, candidate nodegroups: [eu-west-gpu-small us-east-gpu-large], expander=least-wasteful
I0503 12:22:11.567890 packer.go:45] Prefer nodegroup us-east-gpu-large (lower waste) but zone constraints cause pod backfills to fail
```
priya (eng-infra): seems like --expander=least-wasteful is choosing a larger cross-zone nodegroup because it reports lower CPU waste even though zoneAffinity prevents pods landing.
jess (eng-platform): Can you paste the nodegroup autoscaling tags? we recently added different max-pods-per-node values on us-east pool.
marco (eng-infra): eu-west-gpu-small: min=0,max=40,labels: zone=eu-west,k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/node-template/label/gpu-type=a100,priority=100
marco (eng-infra): us-east-gpu-large: min=0,max=200,labels: zone=us-east,gpu-type=a100,priority=10
priya (eng-infra): aha — priority labels are set but our CA config is still using the least-wasteful expander, which ignores priority tags.
autoscaler-bot: [scale-event] scaled up 2 nodes in us-east-gpu-large (reason: most efficient packing) :thumbsup:
jess (eng-platform): Options: 1) switch expander to priority (honors nodegroup priority label) 2) enable --balance-similar-node-groups true 3) add zone constraints to expander via custom priorities 4) add a pre-filter admission that rejects cross-zone provisioning?
priya (eng-infra): I prefer switching to expander=priority + set higher priority on eu-west groups. Also bump --scale-down-unneeded-time to 15m so transient imbalance doesn't immediately downscale.
marco (eng-infra): agree. Also noticed scale-down couldn't remove nodes with local-ds because of our monitoring daemonset. Maybe set --skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false? or consolidate monitoring as a rollout daemonset with tolerations?
jess (eng-platform): CA flags to change proposal: 
```
--expander=priority \
--balance-similar-node-groups=true \
--scale-down-unneeded-time=15m \
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5 \
--max-empty-bulk-delete=10
```
priya (eng-infra): Also add node-group priorities in k8s cloudprovider config: eu-west-gpu-small -> priority: 200, eu-west-gpu-large -> 150, us-east-gpu-large -> 10
marco (eng-infra): one more: set --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true stays true, but audit which DS are running to avoid blocking scale-down.
autoscaler-bot: [test-mode] can simulate policy changes if you send config file to /ops/autoscaler/simulate — run takes ~2m.
priya (eng-infra): I'll run simulate after hours (post 02:00 UTC) to confirm we don't cause oscillations. If simulation looks good, I'll roll CA flags through infra rollout next deploy window.
jess (eng-platform): remember to include the rollout plan in the PR: include metrics to watch (scale events per hour, average pending time, cross-zone node launches) and a quick rollback if pending time worsens.
marco (eng-infra): noted. Also we should add an alert for >3 scale-ups that pick non-preferred zones within 15m.
priya (eng-infra): will add alert to pagerduty runbook. thanks — will post results from simulate. :rocket:
